deleted_rows.name: Cauthorn-Wilson
deleted_rows.fa: Dan Cauthorn and Tim Wilson, April 1984
hazards: Avalanche hazard on these east-facing, sun-exposed slopes — assess snow stability carefully before committing.
Highway 20 access is seasonal, so the approach itself may involve snow travel before or after the road fully opens/closes.
Ice quality varies with recent freeze-thaw; the WI4 crux can be thin in low-snow years.
deleted_rows.overview: A moderate-to-hard early-season ice/mixed line up the obvious big couloir on Cutthroat's East Face: roughly 400 ft of snow/neve leads to a sustained WI4 pitch, easing into several more snow/ice/mixed pitches to the ridge.
deleted_rows.beta: Climb roughly 400 ft of snow/neve to reach a WI3-3+ pitch, then a sustained WI4 crux pitch that eases to WI3+. From the top of the crux, three or four more pitches of snow, ice, or mixed terrain lead to the ridgeline; from there, parties can descend or continue on moderate rock pitches (5.4 in summer conditions) to the true summit.
deleted_rows.permit: No climbing or wilderness permit required; Northwest Forest Pass (or day fee) to park at developed trailheads.
deleted_rows.comms: No cell coverage in this area.
deleted_rows.descent: From the ridgeline, descend via rock anchors (some fixed) or V-threads, or continue on moderate rock pitches to the summit; many parties prefer the West Ridge descent over downclimbing/rappelling the route itself.
obj_haz: avalanche hazard on sun-exposed east-facing slopes
seasonal highway access limits window and can require a snow approach
deleted_rows.detailed_rack: Screws, nuts, pitons, and cams to 1 in., with an emphasis on small gear; two 60m ropes for the technical pitches and descent.
what_to_bring: avalanche assessment gear (given the east-facing, sun-exposed approach)
pro_tips: Climb it right around the highway's seasonal opening/closing when snow/ice conditions are typically best.
West Ridge descent is often preferable to downclimbing/rappelling the route.
Small gear (screws, nuts, pitons, cams to 1 in.) covers the technical sections well.
watch_out: East-facing aspect means significant solar warming during the day — climb early and be off avalanche-prone slopes before it heats up.
Route conditions change quickly season to season; check recent trip reports before committing.
Two 60m ropes are needed for the descent rappels.
deleted_rows.pro_needs: Mixed ice/rock protection — small cams and pitons supplement screws on the rock/mixed sections.
deleted_rows.best_season: Best attempted as soon as possible after Highway 20's spring opening, or right before its fall closure — typically April-May for the most reliable ice/snow conditions.
deleted_rows.approach: Follow the South Buttress approach trail, then traverse over the rib extending south from the South Buttress into the basin east of Cutthroat Peak; the route is the obvious big couloir on the East Face.

access.fees: No fee at the roadside pullout.
access.closures: Highway 20 closes seasonally (roughly Dec-Apr); this route's best window is right at the edges of that closure.
access.landManager: Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Methow Valley Ranger District

road.name: North Cascades Highway (State Route 20)
road.driveNote: Approach via the South Buttress pullout off SR-20; the road may not be fully plowed/open on early-season attempts.
road.seasonalGate: Typically closed roughly early December through mid-to-late April/May depending on snowpack; this route is often climbed right at the edge of that closure window.

emergency.notes: No cell service in this corridor; early-season conditions add avalanche and access risk.
emergency.rangerStation: Methow Valley Ranger District, Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest, Winthrop, WA
emergency.nearestHospital: Three Rivers Hospital, Brewster, WA (critical access hospital)
emergency.sheriffDispatch: Okanogan County Sheriff's Office non-emergency: 509-422-7232 (or 800-572-6604 in-state); call 911 for emergencies

approach_logistics.trailheadDirection: From the long pullout on the north side of SR-20 about 1.5 miles west of Washington Pass, via the South Buttress climbers' trail

approach_variants.name: State Creek approach, then over the rib into the east basin
approach_variants.notes:
Same walk-in as the South Buttress rock routes: the long pullout on the north side of SR-20 about a mile and a half west of Washington Pass, the cairned climbers' track from its east end, down through timber, across State Creek, and up toward the basin south of the peak. Then cross the rib running south from the South Buttress and drop into the basin east of Cutthroat Peak.

The window is set by the highway. SR-20 over Washington Pass is closed each winter, usually from late November or early December until mid-April to early May, and this route is climbed as soon as practical after it reopens.
approach_variants.season: Soon after SR-20 reopens — typically Apr-May
hazards: east aspect in the sun most of the day — avalanche and wet-slide danger
unmarked crossing of the rib into the east basin
very short season tied to the highway reopening
approach_variants.baseFinding: The route takes the big couloir on the East Face, so being in the correct basin is the whole navigation problem — from the east basin the couloir is the obvious dominant gully and cannot be confused with anything else. If the buttresses above you face south and you can see the entry gullies used by the rock routes, you are still on the wrong side of the rib. The climbing starts on snow or névé at the foot of the couloir and steepens gradually to the first ice pitch, so there is no distinct rock feature marking a start.
